description: Iterate over two lists by alternating available values while preserving each list's order. Example 1: [1, 2] and [3, 4, 5, 6] produce 1, 3, 2, 4, 5, 6. Example 2: [1] and an empty list produce only 1. Constraints: each input list contains integers and the total number of calls is finite.
intuition: A queue of active iterators naturally cycles across lists and drops exhausted ones.

brute_force.approach: Materialize the complete alternating output before returning any value.
brute_force.time: construction O(n + m), next O(1), hasNext O(1)

optimal.approach: Queue iterators with remaining elements; pop one, consume a value, then append it again if it is still active.

edge_cases: Either input list may be empty.
Once one iterator is exhausted, the other continues alone.
